agent_notes: Revised after review: removed the claim that no earlier psalm addresses the nations (Ps 47:2, 66:1, 96:7, 100:1 do), and corrected the Targum sentence: it renders both verbs with שבח, so it does not keep them apart. Also dropped the stray 'and' from the gloss of word 6, since the Hebrew has no conjunction there.
Radak (future days of the Messiah) and Malbim (captives of Sennacherib) disagree on the historical setting; the commentary reports both and does not choose.

history.note: [should_fix] In directors_commentary, delete the sentence 'Every psalm before it is sung by Israel, to Israel or about Israel' and the claim that the address to the nations is new; say instead that Psalm 117 compresses into two verses a summons to the nations that the Psalter has made before (e.g. Ps 47:2, 66:1, 96:7, 100:1). (PS.47.2 (KJV 47:1): "O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God"; PS.66.1: "Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands"; PS.96.7: "Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people"; PS.100.1: "Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands".) [should_fix] Rewrite the Targum sentence of the שַׁבְּחוּהוּ note: the Targum uses שבח for both verbs (שַׁבְּחוּ ... שַׁבַּחוּ ליה), so it, like the KJV, does not keep the two Hebrew verbs distinct; keep the Radak citation as it is. (Targum on PS.117.1: "שַׁבְּחוּ יַת יְיָ כָּל עַמַיַא שַׁבַּחוּ לֵיהּ כָּל אוּמַיָא" against the Hebrew "הַֽלְל֣וּ ... שַׁ֝בְּח֗וּהוּ".)

agent_notes: גָּבַר עָלֵינוּ: ASV and KJV render 'great toward us'; YLT 'mighty to us'. The verb is 'to be strong, to prevail', and עַל after it can mean 'over' as well as 'toward'. I kept 'prevailed over us' in the literal layer and 'toward us' as the other possible sense; the choice is mine and the sources are lexicon-level only.

Radak's and Malbim's historical readings (return from exile; Sennacherib's captives) differ, and Meiri and Metzudat David read the psalm as messianic. I did not choose among them in the dramatic layer; the commentary only says that the psalm as written does not name its occasion.
